mechanism_narrative: Sustained four-week upward trend in RETAIL_REC (from -48.7% to -41.3%) indicates recovery momentum in consumer mobility. This trend continues linearly over the next four weeks, producing net positive direction in RETAIL_REC relative to the baseline period.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 7.4 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC four-week mean falls below -41.3% or declines week-on-week in three of the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility recovery (from -43.0% to -37.7%) drives commuting patterns that anchor weekday retail visits. Each percentage-point gain in WORKPLACES within one week produces proportional retail foot traffic lift within the same week.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises above -37.7% in any single week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved 5.3 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: WORKPLACES continues to decline or stagnates below -37.7% while RETAIL_REC simultaneously declines for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Grocery and pharmacy mobility stabilization (declining from -11.6% to -5.0%) signals consumer confidence in essential-service access. This confidence spillover increases discretionary retail visits, with a two-week lag as behavioral adjustment occurs.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM improves by more than 2 percentage points in a single week
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved 6.6 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM reverses to decline below -5.0% while RETAIL_REC remains flat or negative in weeks 2-4 of the forecast period.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT station mobility remains severely depressed (around -70%), constraining access to retail clusters. If TRANSIT fails to recover above -65% within the next two weeks, RETAIL_REC will remain suppressed below -35% due to reduced foot traffic accessibility.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -65% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT shows minimal improvement, only 3.1 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: TRANSIT recovers above -65% in any single week while RETAIL_REC simultaneously declines, or RETAIL_REC rises above -35% despite TRANSIT remaining below -65%.

mechanism_narrative: Joint recovery in WORKPLACES and PARKS mobility (both improving 5+ percentage points) indicates broader social reopening. The interaction of commuting resumption and recreational access creates multiplicative lift in retail visits, with effect emerging over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: both WORKPLACES and PARKS improve by at least 3 percentage points in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved 5.3 points, PARKS improved 14.7 points
failure_condition: Either WORKPLACES or PARKS reverses to decline below their t-0w levels while RETAIL_REC fails to exceed -35% in the forecast period.

mechanism_narrative: Elevated RESIDENTIAL mobility (20-22% above baseline) reflects persistent remote work and home-centered behavior. This constrains retail recovery; the interaction of high RESIDENTIAL with low TRANSIT suppresses RETAIL_REC below -40% over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains above 19% while TRANSIT remains below -68%
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stable at 20-22%, TRANSIT stable at -69 to -72%
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL declines below 18% or TRANSIT recovers above -65% in any week, or RETAIL_REC rises above -38% despite both conditions holding.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent TRANSIT suppression (only 3.1 percentage point improvement over four weeks) indicates ongoing capacity restrictions or service limitations. This policy-driven constraint will prevent RETAIL_REC from recovering above -38% over the next four weeks regardless of other mobility signals.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improvement rate remains below 1 percentage point per week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT weekly improvement averages 0.77 percentage points
failure_condition: TRANSIT improves by more than 5 percentage points in any single week, or RETAIL_REC exceeds -35% in three of the next four weeks despite slow TRANSIT recovery.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-September timing (t-0w = 2021-09-15) marks transition into fall season. Seasonal shift toward indoor retail and recreation activity, combined with observed recovery momentum in RETAIL_REC, produces accelerated gains over the next four weeks as weather cools and back-to-school/fall shopping peaks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS begins declining as seasonal shift occurs (inverse seasonal indicator)
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS declined 14.7 points over four weeks, indicating seasonal shift away from outdoor activity
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to improve by at least 3 percentage points over the next four weeks, or PARKS continues rising instead of declining, indicating seasonal pattern reversal.
